units.text: The Robolectric blog post on android-all downloading on CI says that in recent years, the team has received multiple issues regarding Robolectric's inability to download/resolve the necessary android-all jars when running Robolectric tests in a CI environment.

quotes.quote: In recent years, the team has received multiple issues regarding Robolectric's inability to download/resolve the necessary android-all jars when running Robolectric tests in a CI environment.

units.text: The post says Robolectric downloads the necessary android-all jars using its MavenArtifactFetcher when running Robolectric tests. It says it does not use any proxies defined by the Gradle build system. In a CI environment, especially in environments used by large companies internally, there are often network restrictions that can cause the aforementioned issues.

quotes.quote: Robolectric downloads the necessary android-all jars using its MavenArtifactFetcher when running Robolectric tests. It does not use any proxies defined by the Gradle build system. In a CI environment, especially in environments used by large companies internally, there are often network restrictions that can cause the aforementioned issues.

units.text: Some examples of the issues include "Flaky SHA mismatch on CI builds when retrieving Maven artifacts since upgrading to 4.10.x".

quotes.quote: Some examples include:
Flaky SHA mismatch on CI builds when retrieving Maven artifacts since upgrading to 4.10.x

units.text: The post says Robolectric can load android-all jars from a local directory instead of downloading them from the network when running Robolectric tests, and sets the robolectric.dependency.dir system property to that directory like the following snippet:

quotes.quote: Robolectric can load android-all jars from a local directory instead of downloading them from the network when running Robolectric tests. We can set the robolectric.dependency.dir system property

units.text: - Per the post, when robolectric.dependency.dir is set, Robolectric always looks for android-all jars in that directory and never downloads them, regardless of the value of robolectric.offline.

quotes.quote: When robolectric.dependency.dir is set, Robolectric always looks for android-all jars in that directory and never downloads them, regardless of the value of robolectric.offline.

units.text: - Per the post, if a jar is missing from the directory, the tests fail with a `Path is not a file: ...` error.

quotes.quote: If a jar is missing from the directory, the tests fail with a Path is not a file: ... error.

units.text: - Per the post, if only some environments have these jars, such as CI machines with a pre-populated cache, only set robolectric.dependency.dir in those environments.

quotes.quote: So if only some environments have these jars, such as CI machines with a pre-populated cache, only set robolectric.dependency.dir in those environments.

units.text: - Per the post, robolectric.offline is only useful when robolectric.dependency.dir is not set: setting it to true makes Robolectric look for android-all jars in the test's working directory instead.

quotes.quote: robolectric.offline is only useful when robolectric.dependency.dir is not set: setting it to true makes Robolectric look for android-all jars in the test's working directory instead.

units.text: The post says that to make it work, android-all jars need to be downloaded into the ${rootDir}/robolectric-jars/preinstrumented directory before running any Robolectric tests.

quotes.quote: To make it work, we need to download android-all jars into the ${rootDir}/robolectric-jars/preinstrumented directory before running any Robolectric tests.

units.text: The post says that because Robolectric might add a new android-all jar for a new Android version or modify internal logic to update an existing android-all jar's version, these android-all jars might change across different Robolectric versions.

quotes.quote: Because Robolectric might add a new android-all jar for a new Android version or modify internal logic to update an existing android-all jar's version, these android-all jars might change across different Robolectric versions.

units.text: The post says that if you don't store android-all jars in your Git repository for robolectric.dependency.dir, and you don't want to modify your system properties for Robolectric in your build.gradle.kts, you can try to download android-all jars in a script and download them manually before running any Gradle tasks.

quotes.quote: If you don't store android-all jars in your Git repository for robolectric.dependency.dir, and you don't want to modify your system properties for Robolectric in your build.gradle.kts, you can try to download android-all jars in a script and download them manually before running any Gradle tasks.

units.text: When using SimpleDateFormat#parse() to parse a timezone using the Z marker, Android supports time zones with a colon (i.e. 08:00), while OpenJDK doesn't (i.e. 0800). To work around this:

quotes.quote: When using SimpleDateFormat#parse() to parse a timezone using the Z marker, Android supports time zones with a colon (i.e. 08:00), while OpenJDK doesn't (i.e. 0800).
To work around this:

units.text: - If your min SDK version is 24 or higher, you can use the X marker instead.

quotes.quote: If your min SDK version is 24 or higher, you can use the X marker instead.

units.text: - Use the java.time API, with library desugaring enabled.

quotes.quote: Use the java.time API, with library desugaring enabled.

units.text: - Run the corresponding tests using regular Android tests.

quotes.quote: Run the corresponding tests using regular Android tests.

units.text: When using DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern(String) to create a formatter displaying a short month name (using the MMM pattern), Android will use three-characters names (i.e. Jan), while OpenJDK will use three-characters names followed by a period (i.e. Jan.). In this case, we recommend running the corresponding tests as regular Android tests.

In this case, we recommend running the corresponding tests as regular Android tests.
